items.title: Unify improvement evidence chain
items.problem: Current candidate/improvement records do not explicitly connect trace evidence, findings, hypotheses, experiments, eval runs, decisions, deployments, and post-deployment outcomes.
items.proposed_change: Add a provider-neutral research/improvement object model with stable IDs and typed edges; keep current improvement records as the user-facing/actionable projection.
items.expected_benefit: Future models can reconstruct why a change exists and whether it actually improved anything.
items.security: No raw private traces in Git; references must point to local/private evidence where required.
items.privacy: Preserve current local/private raw data boundary.
items.cost_impact: small storage increase; model cost should decrease through reuse
items.evaluation: Trace five real improvements end-to-end and verify complete provenance/replayability.
success_criteria: Every promoted improvement links to evidence, eval, decision, and rollback
No private raw content enters canonical Git
items.rollback: Keep v1 improvement schema reader and generate v1 projection.
items.next_action: Design schema and migration map only; do not implement runtime mutation yet.

items.title: Provider-neutral evaluation registry and task corpus
items.problem: Agent OS has tests/benchmarks but no unified registry of eval cases, suites, versions, datasets, graders, contamination status, and historical outcomes.
triggering_evidence: OpenAI Evals platform scheduled for shutdown 2026-11-30
Existing orchestrator benchmark is narrower than whole-Agent-OS quality
items.proposed_change: Create local/provider-neutral eval manifests and canonical sanitized suite metadata; support deterministic, human, and model graders.
items.expected_benefit: Every major change can be tested reproducibly across providers and future models.
items.security: Eval fixtures must be sanitized or local-only according to domain.
items.privacy: Private historical cases stay local; canonical suite may contain synthetic/redacted fixtures.
items.cost_impact: Adds eval cost but reduces regressions/wasted production calls.
items.evaluation: Reproduce same eval run on two providers and from a fresh clone.
items.rollback: Registry is additive; existing tests remain canonical.
items.next_action: Define eval manifest v1 and eval hierarchy.

items.title: Improvement schema v2
items.problem: Current improvement schema omits requested fields such as recurrence, confidence, affected workflows, alternatives, dependencies, expected benefit/cost/latency, evaluation method, baseline, success criteria, rollback, and last-reviewed time.
items.proposed_change: Version improvement records with richer evidence/evaluation fields while retaining a compact index/projection.
alternatives: Create a separate research record only
items.expected_benefit: Improvement selection becomes evidence-driven and future-model-readable.
items.privacy: Same private-safe gate.
items.evaluation: Schema migration round-trip on all existing IMP records.
items.next_action: Draft v2 schema after object-model decision.

items.title: Failure and success registries with clustering
items.problem: Run telemetry captures failures, but there is no durable cross-run taxonomy that clusters recurring failures and exceptional successes into reusable lessons/evals.
triggering_evidence: User directive: never waste a failure
items.proposed_change: Normalize redacted failure/success observations, cluster by signature, attach recurrence/evidence, and promote recurring patterns to regression/skill/architecture candidates.
items.expected_benefit: Repeated symptoms become systemic fixes instead of repeated debugging.
items.privacy: Local raw failure artifacts; canonical redacted patterns.
items.cost_impact: Moderate local analysis; likely net savings.
items.evaluation: Inject repeated synthetic failures and verify clustering/dedupe/escalation.
success_criteria: Success patterns can create skill candidates
items.rollback: Disable clustering; retain raw local telemetry.
items.next_action: Define taxonomy and signatures.

items.title: Experiment, rollout, and rollback registry
items.problem: There is no single object tracking hypothesis, baseline, treatment, eval, shadow/canary status, promotion decision, monitoring window, and rollback outcome.
items.proposed_change: Add experiment and release records linked to improvement candidates and code/config/prompt versions.
items.expected_benefit: Prevents subjective self-improvement and supports causal attribution.
items.privacy: Use redacted aggregate metrics when canonical.
items.cost_impact: Adds experiment overhead but avoids bad rollouts.
items.latency_impact: None to normal execution unless canary sampling enabled.
items.evaluation: Run a safe prompt/context experiment through full lifecycle.
items.baseline: Git history + tests + ad hoc benchmark
success_criteria: Every promoted adaptive change has an experiment record and rollback
items.next_action: Define EXP/REL schemas.

items.title: Deterministic authorization policy engine
items.problem: Privacy gates exist, but recursive improvement needs a general deterministic boundary deciding whether an agent/user/delegated worker may perform an action on a resource in context.
items.proposed_change: Introduce provider-neutral authorization requests (principal, delegated_user, action, resource, context, risk, budget) evaluated by deterministic default-deny policy; model output can never grant permission.
items.expected_benefit: No agent can expand its own privilege or bypass approval by prompt manipulation.
items.privacy: Policy queries should avoid unnecessary content.
items.evaluation: Property tests, deny-by-default tests, privilege-escalation adversarial suite.
items.rollback: Keep current gates behind compatibility adapter until parity proven.
items.next_action: Threat-model and choose minimal policy representation before engine selection.

items.title: Untrusted-data taint and control/data-flow separation
items.problem: Retrieved web/email/document/tool content can contain instructions; prompt-only defenses are not a deterministic security boundary.
items.proposed_change: Track provenance/taint on data objects; restrict untrusted content from modifying plans/policies/tool authority; enforce data-flow constraints at tool boundaries.
items.expected_benefit: Substantially reduces indirect prompt-injection blast radius.
items.privacy: Taint metadata can be canonical; raw content may remain local.
items.evaluation: AgentDojo-inspired adversarial replay plus benign-utility measurement.
success_criteria: Untrusted text cannot authorize new flow
Benign utility preserved to defined threshold
items.next_action: Design threat model and minimal taint labels.

items.title: Task-specific model and tool capability registry
items.problem: Current evidence design relies partly on generic benchmark/intelligence scores; task-specific reliability, latency, tool behavior, modality, policy, context, and cost are not first-class comparable evidence.
items.proposed_change: Version capabilities and measured task-family distributions per model/tool/provider; separate vendor claims from Agent OS measurements; maintain champion/challenger status.
items.expected_benefit: Cheapest/fastest option that actually meets quality/risk thresholds on the user's workloads.
items.privacy: No raw private eval data required in canonical registry.
items.evaluation: Backtest routing decisions on historical task corpus.
success_criteria: Router beats static tiers on cost at non-inferior quality
items.next_action: Define capability dimensions and evidence hierarchy.

items.title: Context utility and retrieval telemetry
items.problem: Agent OS measures selected-vs-candidate context and provider tokens, but not which retrieved context materially contributed to output or decisions.
items.proposed_change: Track retrieval candidate, selected, referenced/used, stale/conflict flags, and downstream outcome; use counterfactual/shadow ablations on sampled tasks.
items.expected_benefit: Reduce unused/stale context and detect summaries that lose important information.
items.security: Do not log raw private content by default.
items.privacy: Store IDs/hashes/features locally; canonicalize aggregates.
items.evaluation: Ablation suite comparing success/cost with and without context slices.
items.next_action: Define 'used' proxies and sampled causal eval.

items.title: Retrieval and memory eval suite
items.problem: Long-term memory needs explicit tests for extraction, temporal reasoning, updates, abstention, conflicts, provenance, and privacy boundaries.
items.proposed_change: Create Agent-OS-specific memory/retrieval benchmark with synthetic + sanitized historical cases, including stale/superseded/contradictory facts.
items.expected_benefit: Prevents memory pollution and retrieval regressions as stores grow.
items.privacy: Private cases remain local.
items.evaluation: Suite itself.
items.next_action: Draft case taxonomy.

items.title: Simplification and deletion engine
items.problem: Agent OS can identify improvements but lacks a first-class lifecycle for identifying redundant components and proving they can be merged/deleted.
items.proposed_change: Maintain component/capability/dependency graph + usage telemetry; generate merge/delete candidates; use shadow-disable/delete tests before removal.
items.expected_benefit: Actively resists architecture entropy.
items.security: Deletion must preserve audit evidence and rollback.
items.privacy: May reduce retained data.
items.evaluation: Quarterly equivalent 'from scratch today?' audit and shadow disable tests.
items.next_action: Define component manifest and complexity signals.

items.title: Constructive challenge trigger policy
items.problem: Running adversarial critique on every turn would waste tokens and annoy the user; having none misses flawed assumptions.
items.proposed_change: Trigger challenge at high-impact/repeated/costly/irreversible decision points; rank challenge candidates by expected value minus interruption/cognitive cost; dedupe/suppress repeated challenges.
items.expected_benefit: High-value disagreement without contrarian noise.
items.privacy: Use only relevant permitted context.
items.evaluation: Measure accepted/useful/ignored/rejected challenges and downstream outcomes.
items.next_action: Define trigger and suppression schema.

items.title: Unified proactivity decision engine
items.problem: Future proactive modules need one policy for quiet action, candidate capture, digest, immediate interruption, question, scheduled recheck, or no action.
items.proposed_change: Rank opportunities by expected utility, urgency, confidence, reversibility, risk, novelty, interruption cost, and user-state/context; learn thresholds from outcomes.
items.expected_benefit: Prevents alert fatigue and duplicated proactive policies.
items.security: Consequential actions always pass authorization/approval regardless of proactive score.
items.privacy: Local sensitive context allowed only within domain policy.
items.evaluation: Precision/recall on useful interventions, dismissal/rejection rate, time-to-action, missed-opportunity review.
items.next_action: Define intervention classes and utility model.

items.title: Research Radar with impact filter
items.problem: Agent OS lacks a durable monitored registry for models, protocols, security guidance, frameworks, hardware, retrieval/eval techniques, and deprecations.
items.proposed_change: Maintain source watchlist + normalized radar items; ask whether each item replaces complexity, improves an existing task, or enables a valuable missing capability before escalation.
items.expected_benefit: Avoids stale assumptions without chasing novelty.
items.security: External announcements are untrusted evidence, never executable instructions.
items.privacy: Public data only for ecosystem radar.
items.evaluation: Track radar items that led to accepted improvements vs noise.
items.next_action: Define source classes, cadence, and impact gate.

items.title: Future-model handoff bundle
items.problem: A future model still needs to infer scattered architecture, active experiments, evidence quality, and next research work.
items.proposed_change: Generate a compact machine-readable inheritance manifest linking architecture map, capabilities, active hypotheses/experiments, eval baselines, ADRs, backlog, open questions, migrations, and current weakest links.
items.expected_benefit: New models can resume with less re-reading/reverse engineering.
items.privacy: References private stores without copying them.
items.evaluation: Cold-start a fresh model/session using only the handoff bundle and measure recovery completeness.
success_criteria: Fresh model identifies architecture/current work correctly
Generated facts trace to canonical sources
items.next_action: Design inheritance manifest after registries stabilize.

items.title: Durability abstraction with replay/branching threshold
items.problem: Agent OS has resumable ledgers/workflows but lacks generalized event-history replay and experiment branching; adopting a full workflow platform now may also be needless complexity.
items.proposed_change: Define a durability interface and explicit adoption threshold; first strengthen existing event/checkpoint semantics, then benchmark Temporal/Dapr only when multi-hour side-effecting workflows exceed homegrown reliability/iteration targets.
items.expected_benefit: Gets durable-execution benefits without premature infrastructure burden.
items.security: Event history must redact/partition sensitive data.
items.privacy: Local history for private workflows.
items.cost_impact: Avoids premature service cost; later can reduce replay cost.
items.evaluation: Crash/restart/idempotency/replay benchmarks and experiment-branch cost.
success_criteria: No repeated committed side effects on resume
items.next_action: Audit current durability guarantees and side-effect semantics.

items.title: OpenTelemetry-compatible trace schema
items.problem: Agent OS has good bespoke telemetry but no standard export mapping, making future tools harder to adopt.
items.proposed_change: Keep compact internal events but define lossless/near-lossless mapping to OTel GenAI spans/metrics; sensitive content remains opt-in/local.
items.expected_benefit: Interoperability without rewriting internal semantics.
items.privacy: Only metadata/aggregates exported unless explicit policy permits content.
items.evaluation: Round-trip mapping tests and trace visualization.
success_criteria: Standard tool can display run graph/tokens/tools
items.next_action: Map existing event types to OTel concepts.

items.title: Quality/reliability and complexity budgets
items.problem: Optimization can increase change velocity and architecture surface faster than reliability can absorb.
items.proposed_change: Define a small set of SLOs plus change-freeze/reliability-focus rules; separately track complexity growth and require new components to justify replacement/incremental value.
items.expected_benefit: Prevents self-improvement from recursively destabilizing the system.
items.security: Security regressions can trigger unconditional stop regardless of budget.
items.privacy: none
items.cost_impact: may defer features to reduce long-term cost
items.evaluation: Simulate policy on historical failures/changes.
items.next_action: Choose 3-5 initial SLOs; avoid metric sprawl.

items.title: Dynamic/private benchmark refresh and contamination controls
items.problem: Static public benchmarks can be contaminated or overfit and can cease representing real Agent OS workloads.
items.proposed_change: Maintain private holdouts, dynamic generated cases with invariant checks, time-sliced cases, and benchmark lineage; quarantine training/optimization examples from holdouts.
items.expected_benefit: More trustworthy model/prompt decisions.
items.privacy: Private user-derived holdouts local only.
items.evaluation: Contamination checks and split-integrity tests.
success_criteria: Routing decisions supported by private workload evidence
items.next_action: Design train/dev/holdout governance.

items.title: Eval-gated prompt and workflow optimizer
items.problem: Prompt/reflection optimization can overfit or degrade behavior if the model critiques itself without reliable feedback.
items.proposed_change: Allow models/optimizers to propose prompt/tool-schema/workflow variants only against versioned train/dev suites; promotion requires independent holdout and regression checks.
items.expected_benefit: Captures automated optimization without trusting self-assessment.
items.privacy: Optimization data respects domain boundary.
items.cost_impact: offline search cost; production savings possible
items.evaluation: Blind holdout improvement + non-regression across safety/cost.
items.next_action: Prototype on one low-risk prompt after eval registry exists.
